checked_sources: Independent BFS and all 190 equalizers and 1,048,576 subsets
correctness.rationale: The fixed graph is GP(10,2) with 20 vertices. Independently generated adjacency and all 20 BFS distance rows. Of 190 unordered distinct vertex pairs, ten have empty equalizers and 180 equalizers are exactly unions of two complete antipodal classes; every one of the 45 unordered pairs of the ten classes occurs. A sensor subset resolves iff it occupies at least three classes, because it cannot be contained in an equalizer. Full 2^20 subset count gives 436 nonresolving and 1,048,140 resolving sets, polynomial sum_{j=3}^{10} binom(10,j)(2z+z^2)^j and exactly 960 three-element metric bases. This is exhaustive for one graph, not a sample extrapolation.
residual_risks: The proof is explicitly restricted to this fixed graph; no extension to other generalized Petersen parameters.

value.rationale: The dodecahedron is a classical well-motivated graph; its full resolving polynomial and iff antipodal-pair criterion specify exactly which landmarks distinguish vertices and determine all cardinality counts, including 960 minimum sets. These structural reliability data are not supplied by the known scalar metric dimension, and a natural complete finite invariant can be valuable independently of an infinite family.
residual_risks: No assertion for strong/edge/mixed metric variants or arbitrary graph family.

limitations: Javaid 2008 complete full text unavailable; abstract-only historical originality uncertainty and Oxford vpn_disconnected.
